Subject: Order Form commercial sequencing — invoicing stitch, pricing ramp, and tax onus

Team / Acme procurement,

Thanks for the draft order form. Before legal wrangles it over, I want to confirm the commercial execution plan so Finance and Product ops can wire the invoice templates and entity mapping. Key items we need resolved:

- Pricing ramp: Acme has proposed a 3-stage usage ladder (pilot / ramp / steady state). We need to map SKUs to invoice lines and ensure minimum commits apply per stage (not per invoice period).
- Invoicing waterfall: Proposal is 20% advance at contract signature, then monthly invoices against usage net45. Need confirm if Acme can do 20% upfront or prefer no advance with PO issuance.
- Net terms: Acme has asked for net45 in the past. Redwood standard is net30; we can make net45 an approved exception with credit check and an advance or escrow.
- Taxes: Clarify which party bears VAT/withholding. If Acme supplies tax residency / reverse-charge docs, we can mark invoices accordingly.

I've attached the initial invoice schedule template (invoice_schedule_v3.xlsx) and would like legal to confirm the redline approach for Order Form clauses that reference invoice recipient entity and tax responsibility.

Next steps requested:
1) Kimberly — high level legal flags on entity mapping and withholding.
2) Finance (Ben + Lauren) — operationalize invoice cadence and how we accept tax evidence (SFTP drive vs signed PDF upload).
3) Acme — confirm they can issue a PO and whether they will provide tax residency certificate after signature.

Happy to hop on a short call if that accelerates.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
VP, Commercials & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Order Form commercial sequencing — invoicing stitch, pricing ramp, and tax onus

Markus / team / Acme: 

Quick legal summary of the points that need explicit redlines in the Order Form / MSA: 

1) Invoicing party / remit: the Order Form must list the exact Redwood legal entity that will issue invoices (we should avoid ambiguous "Redwood Inference" phrasing). If Acme needs invoices to "Entity X" we need a signed attestation and an invoice routing appendix.

2) Tax responsibility: standard language — buyer is responsible for taxes, except where buyer provides a valid tax residency or reverse-charge certificate. We should add a timeline: buyer must provide tax evidence within 10 business days of signature; absent evidence, Redwood will invoice gross and collect VAT.

3) Net terms exception: if we agree to net45, require either (a) 20% upfront credit applied to first invoice, or (b) completed credit review and approved payment profile. Recommend (a) for speed.

4) Minimum commits: need a clause tying minimum commit charges to the invoice schedule and specifying proration for mid-period terminations. Also include a one-time reconciliation after quarter-end.

Operational asks for Finance: list of acceptable tax docs (VAT certificate, W-8/W-9, local tax residency). Also confirm where documents should be uploaded — prefer secure SFTP with email receipt.

I'll prepare a short redline for the Order Form (pricing table + invoice remit appendix and tax exhibit). Markus, do you want me to include the 10-business-day evidence window verbatim?

—Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Markus / Kimberly / Ben —

Thanks — Acme can confirm the following from our side:

- We will issue a PO (attached: ACME_PO_12345.pdf) once final Order Form pricing is approved.
- Net45 is our standard. We cannot commit to an upfront cash deposit; if Redwood requires an advance, we need to review the business case internally (unlikely for this enterprise BU).
- We can provide a digital tax residency certificate (we will upload acme_tax_residency_cert.pdf) and we can accept invoices routed to "Acme Cloud Services, Inc." or the subsidiary noted on the PO.
- On entity split: we prefer a single consolidated invoice per month with line items for each SKU; if Redwood must invoice multiple legal entities, we need a short explanation so our AP team can process.

We can do a short call tomorrow AM PT to iron outstanding items if helpful.

Regards,
Emma Torres

Acme Corporation

Thanks everyone — operational proposal from Finance: 

- We can accept Net45 for this account provided Acme issues a PO and we apply a 20% credit (not cash) against the first invoice. The credit will be deducted at invoice generation and any overage/underage will reconcile on the second invoice.
- Invoicing cadence: monthly consolidated invoice with line-level SKUs. If Acme requires entity-split invoices, we can generate split PDFs but they must provide a definitive entity mapping prior to first invoice run.
- Tax evidence: Acceptable docs — VAT registration certificate, tax residency PDF, W-8/W-9. Preferred upload channels: secure SFTP (details to be shared) or encrypted ShareDrive link. We will not accept tax forms via email.
- Attach: invoice_schedule_v3.xlsx (updated with billing entity column). Please review and confirm entity mapping by EOD Friday.

If Acme cannot do the credit approach, we need a short SLA (credit check 48h) and legal to approve net45 language.

—Ben Carter
Director, Revenue Ops

Aim to send redline by Monday COB so Acme can review.
2) Ben / Lauren — share SFTP upload instructions and the updated invoice_schedule_v3.xlsx link (Ben, please push to the related_links drive item). Confirm whether Finance needs any additional commercial terms to accept consolidated invoices with line-level SKUs.
3) Acme (Emma / procurement) — upload tax residency pdf and confirm whether the PO will reference a single invoice recipient or multiple entities. If single, we'll proceed with consolidated monthly invoices.

If there are blocking items after Kimberly's redline I will escalate to GTM leadership for approval. Otherwise we'll target DocuSign signature by next week.

Thanks — Mark
